checks: Matched 0d48b13f5ad2c2a1 §§2–4, (2)–(3). The example concerns a packing maximum over lattice targets and an initially positive weight table, not ordinary atomic depth.

The five given inequalities define the pentagon with the listed extreme points. The lattice census is the sixteen sites in the 4-by-4 grid and the unique extra site (4,2). There are twelve light sites, total weight 501/100, and maximum weight one below 501/400. The only repeated vertex parity is 00 at A,C.

Checked the six disjoint group witnesses using exact barycentric weights. The pair B,E uses weights 2/3 and 1/3, the singleton is m, and the four remaining pairs have midpoint m. Every used capacity is respected and the packing value is 2+4epsilon.

Parsed and independently recomputed all seventeen frozen closed-cap rows from the lattice census, using the inclusive inequality at zero. Each cap must meet every group whose convex hull contains the target, so summing group incidences gives an upper bound by its mass. Targets outside the hull have no group. The exact maximum is 601/300 at m.

For arbitrary 0<delta<=1, changing the A,C pair weight to 1-delta and the singleton weight to epsilon+2delta increases the lower packing value by exactly delta. The same-batch comparison bounds every target by this value. At delta=1 the deleted sites have zero capacity and no positive group uses them; the target m and attaining packing survive.
